title: The Stingray Nebula: The Youngest Known Planetary Nebula (Hen-1357)
caption: The Stingray Nebula (Hen-1357), imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
credit: Matt Bobrowsky (Orbital Sciences Corporation) and NASA

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: A bright central star sits in the middle of a green ring of gas, flanked by gas bubbles at lower left and upper right. Its companion star lies diagonally above it, at the 10 o'clock position, joined by a faint green spur of gas pulled toward it by gravity. Curved red lines trace gas heated by a shock where the star's wind hits the bubble walls. This is the Stingray Nebula, which in 1998 was the youngest known planetary nebula.

A planetary nebula forms when an aging, low-mass star swells into a red giant and blows off outer layers, and the remaining core heats the gas until it glows. The Stingray's central star heated up enough to light its nebula only within the 20 years before 1998, a change that came surprisingly fast for a low-mass star.
The wind from the star has blown holes in the ends of the bubbles, which act like nozzles that steer escaping gas into two opposing streams.
scale: The nebula is as large as 130 solar systems and lies 18,000 light-years away in the direction of the southern constellation Ara, according to NASA.

understand.summary: Taken with Hubble's Wide Field and Planetary Camera 2. F658N (nitrogen) is shown in red, F502N (oxygen) in green and F487N (hydrogen) in blue.
understand.eye: NASA says these are the actual colors emitted by the gases, but from Earth the whole nebula appears only as big as a dime seen from a mile away.

explore: The companion matters because astronomers have suggested a second star may be needed to form the ring, bubbles and columns of gas. The bridge of gas toward it was something never seen before in a planetary nebula. At one-tenth the size of a typical planetary nebula, the Stingray is small, so no details were visible before Hubble observed it.
sources: NASA release: Hubble Reveals Details of a Newly Born Planetary Nebula
alt: A bright star inside a green ring of gas, with bubbles to either side, a companion star at upper left and curved red lines.
